text:
Marcus: Heads-up — we got a renewal ask from FinServe: they want parity with CompetitorX's tool-calling API so they can lift-and-shift. SLA and billing are tied to it.
Anna: Can you paste their ask or example payload?
Marcus: Short version: they want compatible function signatures + structured responses so their integrator won't rewrite. Example payload is basically JSON-RPC-like calls.
Marcus: They also care about latency: <200ms p95 for inference, otherwise they won't move. Renewal is in 6 weeks.
Anna: OK. This is the classic parity vs differentiator decision. Quick thoughts: parity wins short-term renewals, but costs us engineering time and may increase latency/cost.
Josh: Implementing exact API parity means adding a shim + extra serialization steps. That could add ~20-40ms tail and complicate our caching/batching. Also increases memory for function metadata.
Priya: From UX, we can present an adapter that maps CompetitorX payloads to our function-calling model. Users wouldn't see Redwood internals. Minimal surface change.
Emily: Data note — on our eval sets, adding the adapter doesn't change quality, but when we force structured output with strict schemas some models have a 5-7% drop on a few edge prompt clusters. Need regression guardrails.
Jenna: Customer success: FinServe is high-value and will escalate if we can't meet parity. They care more about compatibility than a brand-new Redwood affordance.
Anna: Proposed approach: 1) build an adapter shim that translates CompetitorX calls -> Redwood function calls, 2) ship as opt-in compatibility route, 3) set canary to 5% traffic for 2 weeks, 4) measure latency p95, cost delta, and schema pass rate on their evals.
Josh: Rough eng estimate: 2 full sprints to implement shim + tests + metrics. If we also need an SDK drop, add 1 sprint. We can avoid model retraining.
Marcus: Is there a cheaper option? Something like a hosted translation proxy clients run in their stack?
Priya: That shifts burden to customers and likely hurts renewals. However we could provide an OSS reference proxy as an interim.
Anna: Launch criteria (suggested):
- Latency: end-to-end p95 < 200ms on canary traffic
- Cost: per-token cost delta < 15% vs baseline for same workload
- Quality: no regression > 3% on customer-specified schema tests and our core evals
- Observability: per-route traces + schema validation metrics + rollback auto-on-regress

Marcus: Those look reasonable. FinServe will push for GA before renewal. Can we compress to 1 sprint by deprioritizing SDK?
Josh: Possibly if we scope the shim small and skip deep validation initially. But that increases risk; we'd need quick rollback.
Anna: Risk-managed path: MVP shim + OSS reference proxy in 1 sprint, then SDK + hardened validations in sprint 2. Canary gated by `route:compat-x` and feature flag.
Josh: Agreed. We'll add a routing policy to pin traffic to dedicated infra until canary stabilizes to avoid impacting other customers. Minor infra cost but worth it.
Emily: Add metrics to track: schema_pass_rate, function_call_success, p95_latency, cost_per_1k_tokens, rollback_count.
Priya: UX note — mark the compatibility route as "compatibility mode" in Console and clearly label experimental. Provide migration docs.
Anna: Action items:
- Marcus: confirm FinServe will accept opt-in canary + 2-week GA window (by EOD).
- Josh: draft implementation plan + sprint ask (by tomorrow).
- Priya: write quick docs and migration notes (start today).
- Emily: prepare eval suite and baseline metrics (2 days).
- Jenna: prep customer comms for rollback scenarios.

Marcus: I'll push on the renewal side and try to buy the 2-week runway.
Josh: I'll post a short RFC with the design + perf numbers.
Priya: I'll sketch Console copy and warning flows.
Jenna: I'll coordinate customer expectations.

deploy-bot: deploy-notice: canary route `compat-x` created in staging.
Anna: OK, decision for now: implement compatibility shim as opt-in route, staged canary, prioritized for this customer. If metrics fail launch criteria, rollback and revisit tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
Marcus: :thumbsup:
Josh: Will update RFC in #eng after draft.
Priya: Putting a quick mock in Figma and linking in RFC.
Emily: I'll attach the initial eval CSV to the RFC.
Jenna: Noted. I'll update CS playbook.
Anna: Thanks team — short horizon but possible. We'll reconvene after the RFC review and once Marcus confirms the customer's acceptance.
